image.description: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

item.title: France: Hundreds arrested as student protests escalate
item.description: Student protests have grown in scale and intensity, with violent clashes in some places leading to hundreds of arrests and dozens of injuries.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Gaza: NGO reports dire camp conditions, says Israel is moving 'Yellow Line'
item.description: The Danish Refugee Council alleges that Israel is employing "a policy of protracted displacement" in Gaza. It says the so-called "Yellow Line" is creeping west toward the coast, preventing many from returning home.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
item.description: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers outside the EU. An African partner country has reportedly already been selected.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Are the Houthis winning against Saudi Arabia?
item.description: It's unclear how the Saudis can defuse the threat presented by the Houthis in next-door Yemen or who they can turn to for help. The US isn't interested, the Europeans are hedging and nobody wants open conflict with Iran.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Iran's nuclear program remains shrouded in mystery as the regime debates ditching non-proliferation
item.description: Iran's nuclear program is entering a critical phase as Tehran debates dropping out of a nuclear non-proliferation treaty. Satellite images also show activity at known nuclear sites.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Lawyer of Junaid Hafeez, a Pakistai scholar imprisoned for 13 years, is hopeful for his release
item.description: A former Fullbright scholar, Junaid Hafeez was sentenced to death under Pakistan's controversial blasphemy laws. His family and lawyer told DW there is now hope a court will overturn the conviction.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
item.description: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
item.description: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding.
item.description: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.
item.dc:subject: Culture

item.title: South Korea: Lost shark draws over half a million visitors
item.description: The South Korean port of Busan says that a stranded shark has become a major tourist draw. It's also named the ocean predator an honorary ambassador to the city.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: 'Alternative Nobel' honors women's rights activists, AI researcher
item.description: The Right Livelihood Award has gone to a female AI researcher and women fighting repression. The Sweden-based prize has been dubbed an "alternative Nobel."
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Hungary's reckoning with Orban's corrupt system picks up speed
item.description: Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar vowed to dismantle Orban's corrupt networks. High-profile figures are being arrested and many Hungarians are pushing for swift accountability, but the rule of law takes time.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ethiopia: No regard for civilians as fighting in Tigray continues
item.description: Fighting has returned to northern Ethiopia, shattering a fragile peace in the region. DW spoke to civilians caught in the crossfire amid communication blackouts, as rebel and federal forces keep battling for territory.
item.dc:subject: World
